seed.title: Order and Compliance
seed.description: Find product, assign compliance certificate, create purchase order, take the payment once the user approves it, create the shipment, and send email.
seed.skill:
**Product Order — Certificate-Backed Purchase**

Use this Blueprint when a product order must have a compliance certificate assigned before a purchase order can be created.

The order request arrives with the product already chosen — it comes in from the requesting system, so do not ask which product to order.

Flow: Find product → Check certificate via knowledge lookup → Assign certificate → Create purchase order → Create payment → Customer approval for the charge → [Rejected: cancel the payment, notify, end] → Confirm payment → Create shipment → Send email.

The payment intent is created unconfirmed, so nothing is charged until the user approves it. The approval is a single Customer Approval node that asks the question and then waits: the decision arrives either as the customer's reply in the session or through the session approval endpoint. Only an approved payment is confirmed, shipped and emailed; a rejected one is cancelled and the purchase order stays unpaid.

Exits after emailing confirmation of the completed purchase order, or early with a cancellation notice if the user declines the charge.

seed.title: Meeting Summary A - Full Transcript Only
seed.description: Variant A of the meeting summarizer A/B test. Converts PCM recordings to WAV, transcribes only the mixed meeting-audio recording with includeSpeakerTranscripts disabled, and summarizes that full transcript into an overall summary and the meeting's highlights. The summarizer reads the transcript straight from the transcription step's result through a parameter reference, so the transcript is never retyped or regenerated. It deliberately skips per-speaker transcription, produces no next steps and attributes nothing to individual speakers. The summary is emailed to the meeting participants; the transcript is not judged and nothing is attached.
seed.skill:
**Meeting Recording - Summary Variant A (transcript only)**

Use this Blueprint for the lightweight arm of the summarizer A/B test: only the mixed meeting recording is transcribed, and the summary is written from that full transcript without transcribing each participant's own recording.

Flow: Convert PCM to WAV -> Transcribe only meeting-audio.wav (includeSpeakerTranscripts: false) -> Summarize the full transcript, read by reference from the transcription result (summary + highlights) -> Send email to all participants -> Complete.

Produces a summary and highlights only - no next steps, no speaker transcription, no speaker attribution, no LLM judgement, no attachments and no separate manager email. Exits after emailing the participants.

Sen, toplantı transkriptlerini analiz edip profesyonel toplantı notları çıkaran bir asistansın.

Bu metni analiz et ve sonucu TAMAMEN TÜRKÇE olarak üret.

ALANLAR:
- summary: Toplantının amacını, konuşulan ana konuları ve nasıl sonuçlandığını anlatan 3-5 cümlelik tek bir akıcı paragraf.
- highlights: Toplantıda ele alınan her önemli ana konu için bir kayıt. topic alanına konu başlığını yaz; highlights alanına yalnızca o konuyla ilgili önemli noktaları, talepleri, önerileri ve alınan kararları 1-3 madde halinde yaz.

5. Emin olmadığın bir bilgiyi kesinmiş gibi yazma; belirsiz kalan maddeleri atla.

seed.title: Molfile Intake and SDF Conversion
seed.description: Entry point for files dropped into the enterprise file intake portal. The portal keeps the upload on its own disk and POSTs the metadata (filename, content type, size, checksum, requested target format, the path it wrote the file to, and a download URL) to this blueprint's webhook, which opens a session for the chem file agent. The blueprint uploads the file to S3 itself, under the docs/ prefix, then reads it back out, converts it to SDF and writes it beside the original, under the same base name but with an .sdf extension - the uploaded object itself is never overwritten.
seed.skill:
**Molfile Intake and SDF Conversion — Upload to S3, Convert MOL to SDF**

Use this Blueprint for the intake portal's webhook: it carries the file's `path` on the portal's disk, and the upload to S3 is this Blueprint's job.

Flow: Upload `path` to S3 under `docs/` → read it back out of S3 → convert to SDF → write it beside the original as `.sdf` → Complete.

The upload itself is never overwritten. The flow ends silently at the Complete node.

properties.description: Upload the file the intake portal left on disk into S3, reading it from the path the webhook carried. The portal never talks to AWS - this is where the file enters the bucket. Take path from the webhook and set content_type to the webhook's contentType
properties.instructions: Always store the upload under the docs/ prefix.
properties.label: Upload File to S3

properties.description: Read the file back out of S3 using the bucket and key the upload step reports, so the conversion works on the bytes that actually landed in the bucket
properties.label: Read Uploaded File from S3

properties.description: Convert the MOL blocks that were read from S3 into a single SDF document. The molfile text and the key it was read from are both taken by reference from the read step, so the content is never retyped and the result carries output_key - the same key with the extension swapped for .sdf
properties.label: Convert MOL to SDF

properties.description: Write the converted SDF to S3. Bucket comes by reference from the read step, key and body by reference from the conversion step - output_key and sdf - so the SDF is written beside the upload as a .sdf object with content type chemical/x-mdl-sdfile, and the uploaded .mol key is never touched
properties.label: Write SDF to S3

properties.description: Mark the file intake workflow as complete once the converted SDF has been written to S3
properties.label: Complete

agent.name: chem_file_agent
agent.description: An agent that stores files uploaded through the intake portal in S3 and converts molfiles (MOL) to SDF, writing the result beside the original.

context.userRequest: When a file is uploaded to the intake portal the portal only keeps it on disk and sends us its path; take the webhook, upload that file to S3 first, read it back out, convert it to SDF and write the SDF back to S3 next to the original as a .sdf object, without touching the upload.
